topic.title: The ₹20 crore player can't have a bad day
topic.claim: The IPL auction turned fans into owners; we don't judge a player by his form anymore, we judge him by his price tag.
topic.moment: A big-ticket buy gets out for 12 off 15 balls and the comments read 'crores le liye'; an uncapped kid does the same and gets a heart emoji.

turn.believed: Fans react to how a player performs.
turn.actually: Fans react to how he performs against what he cost, because the auction made the price the first thing we learn about him.

topic.feeling: I'm angry at a player as if it was my money.
topic.villain: An auction broadcast as a show where price becomes the headline
topic.because: The auction is televised and the price sticks to a player all season. Every innings becomes a test of 'was he worth it'.
topic.payoff: Test: remember a player's last score or his auction price. Most of us remember the price.
topic.behaviour: Fans and memes mock costly players after one bad game and celebrate cheap ones for the same output.
topic.mechanism: The price is the first fact we hear, so it becomes the lens for everything after.
topic.group: Cricket fans who follow the IPL
topic.send_to: The friend who called a player 'overpriced' after his first match.
topic.why_now: Auction talk starts before every IPL season and prices become the story again.

score.why: Fans judge a player against his price tag, not his form; it's a shareable argument for any IPL group chat.
